package.name: October 2026 federal-provincial industrial and tariff package
package.summary: On 21 October 2026 the Government of Canada and the Government of Ontario announced $8.72 billion for Ontario steel, Ontario automotive modernization, and a federal contribution to Ring of Fire road access. National programs listed with it (PrairiesCan, the Strategic Response Fund, BDC, and NRCan critical-minerals funds) are separate instruments. An Alberta firm should read the geography on each entry.
composition: Joint Steel Action Fund: $3.55 billion federal and $1.67 billion Ontario over five years ($5.22 billion), for Ontario steel
Ontario automotive modernization: $1.5 billion federal and $1.0 billion Ontario over two years ($2.5 billion)
Ring of Fire road access: up to $1.0 billion federal over three years, matching an Ontario commitment for Northern Ontario

disclaimer: Reading aid only. workspaceAlberta does not apply for funding, contact a department, or decide eligibility. Amounts, intakes, and tests change. Open the official page before relying on a figure.

programs.name: PrairiesCan Regional Tariff Response Initiative
programs.summary: PrairiesCan delivers the national Regional Tariff Response Initiative in Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba. The national envelope is $3.45 billion across regional development agencies, including the $1.5 billion added on 25 August 2026.
programs.amount: Up to $3 million non-repayable for one business ($2 million liquidity and $1 million for a pivot project), and up to $20 million in total RTRI funding. Liquidity is up to 50% of eligible costs. Larger pivot projects can be repayable and interest-free.
programs.eligibility: Tariff-impacted incorporated businesses with at least $1 million in annual revenue, and not-for-profit organizations that help businesses adapt. Intake is open until 31 December 2028 or until funds are committed. Liquidity funding runs no later than 31 March 2028. Pivot projects must finish by 31 March 2029.

programs.name: ISED Strategic Response Fund
programs.administrator: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
programs.summary: National fund for industries facing U.S. tariffs. Since September 2025 it has covered steel, aluminum, automotive, and forest products. On 25 August 2026 it was expanded, including through the Canada Strong Diversification Fund, to industries newly hit by tariffs.
programs.amount: Project size depends on the stream. The Canada Strong Diversification Fund is the capital-maintenance stream inside this fund.
programs.eligibility: Canadian incorporated or registered businesses carrying on business in Canada, in a tariff-affected industry. Alberta firms apply to the national fund. The Ontario Joint Steel Action Fund is a separate Ontario partnership and is not this application.

programs.name: Canada Strong Diversification Fund
programs.administrator: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, as a stream of the Strategic Response Fund
programs.summary: A $2 billion stream of the Strategic Response Fund, announced 25 August 2026, for tariff-impacted firms with shovel-ready capital maintenance so they can keep existing equipment and buildings in service.
programs.amount: Non-repayable funding of $5 million to $30 million, for up to two years, limited to capitalized equipment and building costs.
programs.eligibility: Incorporated or registered in Canada, at least 10 full-time employees, at least $20 million annual revenue, and an average of at least $5 million a year in capital spending over the last three fiscal years. The applicant must show a direct or indirect impact from U.S. Section 338 tariffs.

programs.name: Joint Steel Action Fund
programs.administrator: Government of Canada and the Government of Ontario, using mechanisms such as the Strategic Response Fund
programs.summary: Ontario-only. Five-year commitments of $3.55 billion from Canada and $1.67 billion from Ontario ($5.22 billion) to diversify Ontario steel production, supply defence, advanced manufacturing, energy, and trade infrastructure, and open overseas markets.
programs.amount: $5.22 billion over five years, split $3.55 billion federal and $1.67 billion Ontario.
programs.eligibility: Announced for Ontario's steel industry on 21 October 2026. An Alberta steel firm should use the national Strategic Response Fund, PrairiesCan RTRI, and the BDC metals envelope instead of this Ontario fund.

programs.name: Ontario automotive modernization
programs.administrator: Government of Canada and the Government of Ontario
programs.summary: Ontario-only. Additional capital so Ontario manufacturers can modernize machinery and production lines for connected and electric vehicles.
programs.amount: $2.5 billion over two years: $1.5 billion federal and $1.0 billion from Ontario.
programs.eligibility: Announced 21 October 2026 for Ontario's automotive industry. It is not an Alberta application stream.

programs.name: BDC Pivot to Grow
programs.summary: National BDC financing for Canadian businesses adapting to tariffs, including working capital, equipment, and a liquidity stream. The 25 August 2026 package added a $500 million liquidity stream under Pivot to Grow.
programs.amount: Financing up to $5 million is the published working range for Pivot to Grow loans, equipment, and liquidity. Terms such as interest-only periods vary by product.
programs.eligibility: Canadian businesses, generally at least $1 million in revenue and at least three years in operation, with tariff or U.S. export exposure. BDC confirms the exact test on the application. Available to Alberta firms in any sector that meets those tests.

programs.name: BDC metals envelope (Steel and Aluminium Industries Support Program)
programs.summary: National metals envelope inside BDC's tariff response. BDC describes it as the Steel and Aluminium Industries Support Program: working capital for steel, aluminium, copper, and fabricated-product manufacturers that export to the United States.
programs.amount: A $1 billion financing mandate. Working capital from $250,000 to $50 million.
programs.eligibility: Canadian-based manufacturers in the steel, aluminium, or copper value chain, exporting to the United States, at least $1 million in revenue and at least three years in operation, viable before the tariff measures. An Alberta fabricator that matches those facts can ask BDC. It is not limited to Ontario.

programs.name: NRCan First and Last Mile Fund
programs.summary: National fund of up to $1.5 billion until 2030 for strategic mining and the roads, power, and site work that get critical minerals to market. It subsumes the Critical Minerals Infrastructure Fund. There is no open call. NRCan invites projects.
programs.amount: Up to $1.5 billion in federal funding until 2030. Contribution size is set per invited project.
programs.eligibility: Strategic Canadian critical-minerals projects, including mine development, enabling transport and clean energy, onward market access, and Indigenous participation. Alberta projects can be put forward through provincial and federal identification. The October 2026 Ring of Fire road money is a separate Ontario infrastructure commitment, not this application form.

programs.name: Canada Critical Minerals Accelerator
programs.summary: National instrument for strategic critical-minerals projects moving toward production. The 21 October 2026 announcement tells Canada and Ontario to identify Ring of Fire projects that could use it, alongside the First and Last Mile Fund. That Ring of Fire use is Ontario-specific. The accelerator itself is not an Ontario-only program.
programs.amount: Not a published open intake with a fixed cheque size. Support is identified project by project, with other federal tools such as investment tax credits.
programs.eligibility: Priority Canadian critical-minerals projects. There is no public application portal to treat as open. An Alberta proponent needs the project identified with Natural Resources Canada and the province. Do not read the Ring of Fire shortlist as the only door.

programs.name: PSPC Buy Canadian Policy Framework
programs.summary: Procurement policy, not a grant. The Buy Canadian Procurement Policy Framework took effect on 16 December 2025. It is the parent of the materials policy, the strategic-supplier and Canadian-content policy, and it sits beside the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement.
programs.amount: No funding cheque. On covered federal procurements, Canadian materials can be mandatory, and Canadian suppliers and Canadian content can receive evaluation preference.
programs.eligibility: Canadian suppliers, including Alberta businesses, bidding on in-scope federal contracts. The materials policy applies to defence goods and construction at $25 million or more where Canadian steel, aluminum, or wood of at least $250,000 is required and Canadian supply exists. The strategic policy applies at $5 million or more as of 15 June 2026. Reciprocal procurement limits non-defence access to Canada and trading partners that give equivalent access.

programs.name: Buy Ontario Policy
programs.summary: Ontario-only procurement policy. The 21 October 2026 announcement pairs it with the federal Buy Canadian Policy to prefer Canadian and Ontario steel in Ontario public buying.
programs.amount: No Alberta funding stream. It changes how Ontario public buyers prefer Ontario and Canadian goods.
programs.eligibility: Applies to Ontario public procurement, not to Alberta Purchasing Connection or to a federal notice that an Alberta firm is bidding.

programs.name: Ring of Fire road access
programs.administrator: Government of Canada and the Government of Ontario
programs.summary: Ontario-only infrastructure. Canada committed up to $1 billion over three years to match Ontario's initial investment in roads that reach the Ring of Fire in Northern Ontario.
programs.amount: Up to $1 billion federal over three years, matching an Ontario commitment of up to $1 billion. This provincial match is infrastructure for Northern Ontario, not a national minerals fund.
programs.eligibility: Road and related access for Northern Ontario's Ring of Fire. An Alberta critical-minerals project is not this road. Use the First and Last Mile Fund and the Critical Minerals Accelerator entries for national instruments.
